documents.title: AI Syllabus Statements
documents.stance_why: The provost document tells instructors to "communicate the extent to which AI use is permitted overall" and gives three degrees of AI use with sample statements for each. It sets no single stance and offers tiers, so stance is delegates.
documents.summary: This Mizzou provost document is a menu of three tiers (prohibited, limited, integration allowed) with sample syllabus language and citation formats for instructors to pick from. It sets no university stance of its own.

units.why: The page tells instructors to "communicate the extent to which AI use is permitted overall", so it is a rule that each course states its AI stance; instructor, course-start, should, type P09 (state AI expectations in the syllabus).
units.anchor: communicate the extent to which AI use is permitted overall

units.why: "review examples of transparency guidelines that describe citation and attribution practices" advises instructors who allow AI to set disclosure guidelines; P24 (disclosure) is nearest, should for instructors.
units.anchor: review examples of transparency guidelines that describe citation and attribution practices
units.frag_start: If AI is allowed to any
units.fit_note: Addressed to instructors: they should provide transparency guidelines; it does not itself require students to disclose.

units.why: "Find helpful icons for all AI positions to use on your syllabi and assignments" points instructors to icons for marking each AI position on syllabi; P09 (state expectations in syllabus) fits best because P05 would be the tiers themselves.
units.anchor: Find helpful icons for all AI positions to use on your syllabi and assignments
units.fit_note: Optional visual icons for communicating the AI position; not a requirement to state it.

units.why: The table names a tier "AI tools are not allowed for any assignments" under "AI Usage Prohibited"; this is a named level of AI use, so P05, instructors choose it, informs.
units.anchor: AI tools are not allowed for any assignments.
units.policy: One tier instructors may adopt is AI Usage Prohibited: AI tools are not allowed for any assignments.

units.why: The second tier is "AI tools are allowed for specific assignments or tasks, as designated by the instructor, with proper citation" (Limited AI Usage Permitted); a named level, P05.
units.anchor: allowed for specific assignments or tasks, as designated by the instructor
units.policy: One tier instructors may adopt is Limited AI Usage Permitted: AI tools are allowed for specific assignments or tasks, as designated by the instructor, with proper citation.

units.why: The third tier "AI tools can be used broadly with ethical guidelines and proper citation" (AI Integration Allowed) is the most permissive named level; P05.
units.anchor: AI tools can be used broadly with ethical guidelines and proper citation.
units.policy: One tier instructors may adopt is AI Integration Allowed: AI tools can be used broadly with ethical guidelines and proper citation.

units.why: The sample says "a strict policy against the use of AI software in any aspect of the learning process"; a course-wide ban is P01 and it binds students.
units.anchor: strict policy against the use of AI software in any aspect of the learning process

units.why: "Students are expected to rely solely on their own cognitive abilities and academic skills when drafting, editing, and revising" bars AI help with producing and revising work; P19 (do not have AI produce the work) fits, not P21 because it covers all drafting.
units.anchor: rely solely on their own cognitive abilities and academic skills when drafting, editing, and revising

units.why: The sample gives the reason "to ensure that assessments accurately reflect each student's independent learning and writing capabilities", an honest-evaluation rationale rather than a skill-building one, so P95.
units.anchor: ensure that assessments accurately reflect each student’s independent learning and writing capabilities

units.why: "This policy aligns with the UM System Student Code of Conduct 200.010" ties the course ban to existing university rules, P77.
units.anchor: This policy aligns with the UM System Student Code of Conduct 200.010.

units.why: "Unless students are explicitly told otherwise, this course prohibits generative AI" states what applies when nothing else is said, the fallback rule P06.
units.anchor: Unless students are explicitly told otherwise, this course prohibits generative AI.

units.why: "Assignments aim to develop your skills" explains the ban by the skill-building purpose of assignments, P41.
units.anchor: Assignments aim to develop your skills.

units.why: "Maintain evidence of your work (drafts, notes, sources) to demonstrate originality" directs students to keep drafts and notes; P26 (keep drafts) fits, as a should.
units.anchor: Maintain evidence of your work (drafts, notes, sources) to demonstrate originality.
units.fit_note: Drafts are kept as proof of originality in a no-AI course, not to document AI use.

units.why: "Violations of this policy will constitute academic integrity violations under University rules" classifies breaches as misconduct, P36.
units.anchor: Violations of this policy will constitute academic integrity violations under University rules.

units.why: "The use of any form of Generative AI is not permitted in this course" is a blanket course ban, P01.
units.anchor: The use of any form of Generative AI is not permitted in this course.

units.why: "The assignments have been designed to ensure that you personally develop and demonstrate the knowledge and skills" gives the skill-building reason, P41.
units.anchor: ensure that you personally develop and demonstrate the knowledge and skills
units.frag_end: outcomes laid out in the syllabus.

units.why: "you are encouraged to maintain clear evidence of your work (e.g., time-stamped drafts and notes" recommends keeping drafts to show ownership; P26.
units.anchor: you are encouraged to maintain clear evidence of your work (e.g., time-stamped drafts and notes
units.fit_note: Drafts are kept as proof of ownership in a no-AI course, not to document AI use.

units.why: "Any violation of these rules will be treated as academic dishonesty punishable under University rules" classifies violations as misconduct, P36.
units.anchor: Any violation of these rules will be treated as academic dishonesty punishable under University rules.

units.why: "Generative AI may be used with prior instructor permission and appropriate attribution" makes use depend on the instructor's permission, so P04 (instructor decides); attribution is coded separately.
units.anchor: Generative AI may be used with prior instructor permission

units.why: "You may use Generative AI tools for productivity in this course" is a general permission within the limited-use sample, P02.
units.anchor: You may use Generative AI tools for productivity in this course.
units.fit_note: The permission is for 'productivity', inside a statement that otherwise requires instructor permission.

units.why: "In class, we will cover how Generative AI is used within this discipline" says the course teaches AI use, P44.
units.anchor: we will cover how Generative AI is used within this discipline

units.why: "Take responsibility for the content" makes students answerable for what they submit, P29.
units.anchor: Take responsibility for the content

units.why: "AI can produce content that contains inaccurate information, offensive language/images, and biased or unethical representations" warns that output is flawed, P31.
units.anchor: AI can produce content that contains inaccurate information, offensive language/images

units.why: "What you submit is your responsibility across these dimensions" restates ownership of the submission, P29.
units.anchor: What you submit is your responsibility across these dimensions.

units.why: "Provide clear attribution of your sources" requires disclosure of AI use, P24.
units.anchor: Provide clear attribution of your sources.

units.why: "Any assignments that utilize Generative AI without attribution ... can be seen as potential academic dishonesty" makes failing to attribute the violation, P28.
units.anchor: Generative AI without attribution pursuant to the guidelines shared in this course
units.policy: Assignments that use generative AI without attribution under the course guidelines can be seen as potential academic dishonesty punishable under University rules.

units.why: "Review individual assignments to determine permissible uses" leaves AI permission to each assignment, P04.
units.anchor: Review individual assignments to determine permissible uses.

units.why: "you should be able to demonstrate how you contributed to an assignment" asks students to show their own contribution; P30 is the nearest type.
units.anchor: you should be able to demonstrate how you contributed to an assignment
units.fit_note: Demonstrate one's own contribution, not explain each line.

units.why: "you are required to keep drafts of assignments and generative AI logs" is offered as an example faculty requirement for logs of AI use, P26.
units.anchor: keep drafts of assignments and generative AI logs that demonstrate how you used AI
units.fit_note: Given as an example that faculty may add.

units.why: "AI software is permitted solely for brainstorming and idea generation purposes" permits one narrow use, P15.
units.anchor: AI software is permitted solely for brainstorming and idea generation purposes.
units.frag_end: generate initial ideas for their writing assignments.

units.why: "the actual writing, drafting, and editing processes must be completed without AI assistance" bars AI from producing the submitted prose, P19 (not P18 because it is the ban itself).
units.anchor: the actual writing, drafting, and editing processes must be completed without AI assistance

units.why: "We encourage the use of AI software in this writing-intensive course" welcomes AI use by default, P02.
units.anchor: We encourage the use of AI software in this writing-intensive course

units.why: "leverage these tools for drafting and editing their assignments" allows AI for writing support, P91.
units.anchor: leverage these tools for drafting and editing their assignments

units.why: "students must provide transparent notes regarding the AI's suggestions and corrections" requires a disclosure note with the submission, P24.
units.anchor: students must provide transparent notes regarding the AI’s suggestions and corrections

units.why: "foster collaboration between students and AI" frames AI as a collaborator under integrity expectations, P45.
units.anchor: foster collaboration between students and AI
units.fit_note: Names collaboration with AI as an aim, with acknowledgement of outside assistance.

units.why: "Proper citation is expected for all sources, however" asks for citation of AI as a source, P24.
units.anchor: Proper citation is expected for all sources

units.why: "Failure to follow these guidelines will constitute an academic integrity violation under University rules" makes nondisclosure a violation, P28.
units.anchor: Failure to follow these guidelines will constitute an academic integrity violation under University rules.

units.why: "The content you submit is your responsibility" makes students own submitted work, P29.
units.anchor: The content you submit is your responsibility.

units.why: "AI-generated content can be inaccurate, offensive, and biased" warns that output must be checked, P31.
units.anchor: AI-generated content can be inaccurate, offensive, and biased.

units.why: "Be sure your work accurately reflects your understanding and avoids these pitfalls" tells students to check AI output so it is accurate, P31.
units.anchor: Be sure your work accurately reflects your understanding and avoids these pitfalls.

units.why: "Generative AI will be integrated into this course" builds AI into the course, P79.
units.anchor: Generative AI will be integrated into this course.

units.why: "Assignments in this course have been purposefully designed to integrate Generative AI in support of the learning objectives" is a redesign of assignments around AI, P35.
units.anchor: Assignments in this course have been purposefully designed to integrate Generative AI

units.why: "we will discuss how Generative AI is used within this discipline" says the course will teach and discuss AI use, P44.
units.anchor: In class, we will discuss how Generative AI is used within this discipline

units.why: "students shall give credit to AI tools whenever used, even if only to generate ideas" requires disclosure of any use, P24.
units.anchor: students shall give credit to AI tools whenever used, even if only to generate ideas

units.why: "add an appendix showing (a) the entire exchange" requires the full transcript, P26.
units.anchor: add an appendix showing (a) the entire exchange, highlighting the most relevant sections

units.why: "(b) a description of precisely which AI tools were used" names the tool in the citation, P25.
units.anchor: a description of precisely which AI tools were used

units.why: "(c) an explanation of how the AI tools were used" requires an account of the use, P24 as it is disclosure of how AI was used.
units.anchor: an explanation of how the AI tools were used

units.why: "(d) an account of why AI tools were used" asks for a reflection on motive, P26 (reflections).
units.anchor: an account of why AI tools were used

units.why: The template "I acknowledge the use of AI in completing this assignment" is an AI statement attached to the submission, P24.
units.anchor: I acknowledge the use of AI in completing this assignment
units.policy: Students acknowledge the use of AI in completing the assignment with a brief explanation of how they used it.

units.why: "I crafted the following prompts: [List prompts used]" has students list the prompts, P25.
units.anchor: I crafted the following prompts: [List prompts used]

units.why: "clearly attribute what text was generated by the AI tool" marks AI text where it appears in the submission, P27.
units.anchor: clearly attribute what text was generated by the AI tool

units.why: "using AI-content generation tools is permitted and will be a normal and regular part of our creative process" welcomes AI use in a design course, P02.
units.anchor: using AI-content generation tools is permitted and will be a normal and regular part

units.why: "neglecting to follow these requirements may be considered academic dishonesty" makes missing citation the violation, P28.
units.anchor: neglecting to follow these requirements may be considered academic dishonesty

units.why: "explains what AI content- generation tool you used, the dates you used it, and the prompts" requires tool, dates and prompts, P25.
units.anchor: what AI content- generation tool you used, the dates you used it, and the prompts

units.why: "cite that image or content following the MLA style guide" requires citation of AI-generated images in critique, P24.
units.anchor: cite that image or content following the MLA style guide

units.why: "Provide the name of the AI tool, the date of access, the URL of the interface, and the specific prompt" lists citation details, P25.
units.anchor: the name of the AI tool, the date of access, the URL of the interface
units.frag_end: or query you used to generate the output.

units.why: "Cite any AI tools you use properly, following the citation style specified by the instructor" requires citing AI use, P24.
units.anchor: Cite any AI tools you use properly, following the citation style specified by the instructor

documents.title: What is the University of Missouri System's policy on student AI use?
documents.stance_why: The System "has decided to leave to each individual faculty member or their departments the decision", so the document delegates. It also states a fallback that AI is forbidden if not clearly allowed, and a stoplight set of tiers.
documents.summary: The UM System page leaves the decision on student AI use to faculty or departments, with a fallback that AI is forbidden when not clearly allowed. It offers a red/yellow/green framework and advice on setting and communicating the policy.

units.why: "decided to leave to each individual faculty member or their departments the decision" hands the AI decision to instructors or departments, P04.
units.anchor: leave to each individual faculty member or their departments the decision
units.frag_start: the University of Missouri System has

units.why: "if an instructor does not clearly allow the use of generative AI, it is forbidden" is the fallback rule when the syllabus does not allow AI, P06.
units.anchor: if an instructor does not clearly allow the use of generative AI, it is forbidden

units.why: "each individual instructor is best equipped to judge and decide what role generative AI should play" gives the reason for delegating, P04.
units.anchor: each individual instructor is best equipped to judge and decide what role generative AI should
units.fit_note: States the reason the System delegates, not the delegation itself.

units.why: "They cannot and should not use this technology to any extent or for any purpose" defines the Red light level, P05.
units.anchor: They cannot and should not use this technology to any extent or for any purpose.
units.policy: Red light: students stop; they cannot and should not use AI to any extent or for any purpose.

units.why: "They can use this technology in certain contexts and for certain purposes" defines the Yellow light level, P05.
units.anchor: They can use this technology in certain contexts and for certain purposes.
units.policy: Yellow light: students proceed with caution; they can use AI in certain contexts and for certain purposes, only somewhat and under the instructor's specific conditions.

units.why: "They can use this technology throughout their learning and with any assessment if they so wish" defines the Green light level, P05.
units.anchor: use this technology throughout their learning and with any assessment
units.policy: Green light: students go; they can use AI throughout their learning and with any assessment if they wish.

units.why: "students should remain a “human in the loop,” reviewing and taking ownership of their work" applies even under green light, P29.
units.anchor: students should remain a “human in the loop,” reviewing and taking ownership of their work

units.why: "given concerns about the accuracy and biases of these tools" is the reason for review, P31.
units.anchor: given concerns about the accuracy and biases of these tools

units.why: "You should always begin with your learning objectives when considering what policy to adopt" ties the policy to objectives, P83.
units.anchor: You should always begin with your learning objectives when considering what policy to adopt

units.why: "help students build 21st century skills, such as creativity and communication" frames AI as building skills, P44.
units.anchor: help students build 21st century skills, such as creativity and communication
units.frag_start: How would using generative AI help

units.why: "is a helpful framework for thinking about the extent to which you would like to let students use this technology" recommends a scale of AI use, P05.
units.anchor: is a helpful framework for thinking about the extent to which
units.frag_end: this technology in their learning and with assessments.

units.why: "Introduce it at the beginning of the semester" tells instructors to communicate the policy at the start; P09 nearest.
units.anchor: Introduce it at the beginning of the semester.
units.fit_note: Timing: introduce the policy in week one; not specifically in the syllabus.

units.why: "The syllabus for a class should include a section discussing generative AI" asks for an AI section in the syllabus, P09.
units.anchor: The syllabus for a class should include a section discussing generative AI
units.frag_start: The syllabus for a class should

units.why: "if you teach at Mizzou, you are required to include a syllabus statement on AI use" makes the statement mandatory, P09.
units.anchor: you are required to include a syllabus statement on AI use
units.frag_start: As a matter of fact, if

units.why: "identify and describe the contexts (when, where, how, why and for what) students can use" asks for specific contexts in the statement, P09.
units.anchor: identify and describe the contexts (when, where, how, why and for what) students can use
units.fit_note: Adds what the statement must contain: when, where, how, why and for what.

units.why: "instructors could engage students in a conversation about generative AI" goes beyond the syllabus text, P66.
units.anchor: instructors could engage students in a conversation about generative AI

units.why: "collaborate with students in each course you teach to develop the expectations" suggests co-creating the policy, P67.
units.anchor: collaborate with students in each course you teach to develop the expectations
units.frag_end: surrounding the use of generative AI.

units.why: "Involving students in the process of developing the AI policy will build goodwill and encourage compliance" gives the benefit of co-creation, P67.
units.anchor: Involving students in the process of developing the AI policy will build goodwill

units.why: "reiterating and reinforcing your policy when introducing new assessments" advises repeating the rule during the term, which no type covers.
units.anchor: reiterating and reinforcing your policy when introducing new assessments
units.uncovered_note: Instructors should repeat and reinforce their AI policy throughout the semester, especially when introducing new assessments.

units.why: "Your students might need to navigate several different AI policies across the classes they are taking" notes that policies vary by course, P11 nearest.
units.anchor: Your students might need to navigate several different AI policies across the classes
units.frag_end: across the classes they are taking
units.fit_note: Observes that rules differ across courses as a reason to repeat the policy; it does not say one course's rules do not carry over.

units.why: "invite students to participate in a discussion about how AI could play a unique, appropriate and ethical role with each individual assessment" is a class discussion of AI per assessment, P66.
units.anchor: invite students to participate in a discussion about how AI could play a unique

units.why: "It is impossible to ensure that students will comply with the policy you have set" states a limit of control, P82.
units.anchor: It is impossible to ensure that students will comply with the policy you have set

units.why: "Proctoring solutions might mitigate the use of this technology, but some might debate and question the use of surveillance technologies" notes proctoring as a partial and contested remedy; P82 is nearest.
units.anchor: Proctoring solutions might mitigate the use of this technology
units.fit_note: Also raises the objection to proctoring as surveillance.

units.why: "With effective instruction and well-designed assessments, you can prevent the risk of students" says better teaching reduces the temptation, P99.
units.anchor: With effective instruction and well-designed assessments, you can prevent the risk of students

units.why: "enrolling in and completing the “Academic integrity in the age of AI” sprint" points instructors to training, P63.
units.anchor: enrolling in and completing the “Academic integrity in the age of AI” sprint

documents.title: ChatGPT, Artificial Intelligence, and Academic Integrity
documents.stance_why: AI is allowed only with the instructor's permission: "using ChatGPT on assignments is prohibited if the instructor does not allow its use". It is restrict: banned unless permitted, with the unauthorized-use rule in the Standard of Conduct.
documents.summary: The Office of Academic Integrity page tells students that using ChatGPT or similar tools without permission, or improperly, is academic dishonesty. It explains the August 2023 Standard of Conduct language and tells students to ask the instructor when unsure.

units.why: "Students who use ChatGPT and similar tools on assignments without permission, or who use them in improper ways, are violating the academic integrity rules" classifies unpermitted use as misconduct, P36.
units.anchor: Students who use ChatGPT and similar tools on assignments without permission

units.why: "If your professor allows you to use ChatGPT, and you use it as permitted, then you are not committing academic dishonesty" makes permission the instructor's, P04.
units.anchor: If your professor allows you to use ChatGPT, and you use it as permitted

units.why: "using ChatGPT on assignments is prohibited if the instructor does not allow its use" is a fallback rule, P06.
units.anchor: using ChatGPT on assignments is prohibited if the instructor does not allow its use
units.frag_start: Just like a graphing calculator, however,

units.why: "This is similar to use of a graphing calculator, which is acceptable as long as the instructor permits it" is a tool analogy that fits no type.
units.anchor: a graphing calculator, which is acceptable as long as the instructor permits it
units.uncovered_note: Likens AI to a graphing calculator that is acceptable only when the instructor permits it.

units.why: "Any effort to gain an advantage not given to all students is dishonest" grounds the rule in fairness, P95.
units.anchor: Any effort to gain an advantage not given to all students is dishonest
units.frag_end: or not the effort is successful.

units.why: "Students who use ChatGPT and similar programs improperly are seeking to gain an unfair advantage" explains the unfairness, P95.
units.anchor: seeking to gain an unfair advantage, which means they are committing academic dishonesty

units.why: "the University of Missouri explicitly prohibits “unauthorized use of artificially generated content,”" states the Standard of Conduct rule, P36.
units.anchor: explicitly prohibits “unauthorized use of artificially generated content,”

units.why: "taking quizzes, tests, examinations, or other assessments without permission from the instructor" bars unpermitted AI on assessments, P22.
units.anchor: taking quizzes, tests, examinations, or other assessments without permission from the instructor

units.why: "submitting work for evaluation as one’s own that was produced in material or substantial part through use of artificial intelligence tools" bars unpermitted AI-produced work, P19.
units.anchor: submitting work for evaluation as one’s own that was produced in material or substantial part

units.why: "Tools exist that aim to detect text created by ChatGPT and similar programs" says detectors are used, P40.
units.anchor: Tools exist that aim to detect text created by ChatGPT and similar programs.

units.why: "the tools that create text will evolve over time, as will the tools designed to detect AI-created text" says both generators and detectors will keep changing, P82 nearest.
units.anchor: the tools that create text will evolve over time, as will the tools designed
units.fit_note: Says detection changes with the tools; it does not say bans cannot be enforced.

units.why: "students deny themselves the benefit of learning new material" gives the learning reason, P41.
units.anchor: by undermining the purpose of assignments, students deny themselves the benefit of learning new material
units.frag_end: purpose of taking university courses in the first place.

units.why: "If you think your instructor would object to your using ChatGPT (or a similar tool) in a certain way, you should not do it" tells students to hold back when objection is likely, P10.
units.anchor: If you think your instructor would object to your using ChatGPT

units.why: "If you are unsure, you should ask your instructor first" is the ask-first rule, P10.
units.anchor: If you are unsure, you should ask your instructor first.

units.why: "If the instructor approves your plan to use an AI tool, then you are not acting dishonestly" says approval removes the integrity problem, P04.
units.anchor: If the instructor approves your plan to use an AI tool

units.why: "If you have any doubt, tell your instructor what tools you used and how you used them" asks for disclosure to the instructor, P24.
units.anchor: tell your instructor what tools you used and how you used them

units.why: The Honor Pledge "I have neither given nor received unauthorized assistance on this work" binds students to unauthorized-assistance limits, P29 nearest.
units.anchor: I have neither given nor received unauthorized assistance on this work
units.fit_note: General honor pledge applied to AI; not specific to AI.

units.why: "students should commit to doing their own work, without “unauthorized assistance” from humans or machines" ties AI to doing one's own work, P29.
units.anchor: students should commit to doing their own work, without “unauthorized assistance” from humans or machines

units.why: "There are legitimate ways to use these tools for research" acknowledges legitimate use; P02 is the nearest type.
units.anchor: There are legitimate ways to use these tools for research
units.fit_note: Only says legitimate uses exist; it does not state a default.

documents.title: Artificial Intelligence Policy for Graduate Education
documents.stance_why: The Graduate School sets no AI stance itself: "Academic units will create policies" for coursework, research, exams and capstones, choosing among restricting, permitting some, or permitting all uses. So it delegates.
documents.summary: The Graduate School requires academic units to write their own AI policies for four areas of graduate education, each stating goals, whether AI is permitted, which tasks and tools, and disclosure. It lists what coursework, research, exams and capstones must have.

units.why: "Academic units will create policies related to the use of AI ... relevant for their disciplines" assigns policy-making to academic units, P85.
units.anchor: Academic units will create policies related to the use of AI

units.why: The list "organized coursework, 2) supervised research ... 3) qualifying and comprehensive exams, and 4) capstone experiences" sets the scope of the policy, P61.
units.anchor: organized coursework, 2) supervised research (or other supervised creative endeavors), 3) qualifying and comprehensive exams
units.fit_note: Defines the scope as four areas of graduate education rather than defining AI.

units.why: "The goal(s) of the educational experience" is a required element of each policy, tying it to goals, P83.
units.anchor: The goal(s) of the educational experience.

units.why: "Whether AI is permitted" is a required element of every unit policy, so each must state its stance, P09.
units.anchor: Whether AI is permitted
units.fit_note: Applies to unit policies for coursework, research, exams and capstones, not only syllabi.

units.why: "which tasks (and tools, if applicable) are permitted" requires the policy to list allowed tasks and tools, P09.
units.anchor: which tasks (and tools, if applicable) are permitted.

units.why: "how AI use should be disclosed and acknowledged" requires the policy to set disclosure rules, P24.
units.anchor: how AI use should be disclosed and acknowledged.
units.fit_note: Units must specify disclosure; it does not itself require students to disclose.

units.why: "restrict all uses of AI, permit some uses of AI, or permit all uses of AI" sets three options, P05.
units.anchor: restrict all uses of AI, permit some uses of AI, or permit all uses

units.why: "must be compliant with ethical, research, and IT guidelines" requires unit policies to follow university rules, P77.
units.anchor: All policies created by academic units must be compliant with ethical, research, and IT guidelines

units.why: "improper uses of AI is academic dishonesty" classifies misuse as misconduct, P36.
units.anchor: improper uses of AI is academic dishonesty

units.why: "faculty will follow the procedures of that office" sends suspected cases to the Office of Academic Integrity process, P81.
units.anchor: in cases of suspected academic dishonesty, faculty will follow the procedures of that office

units.why: "Individual programs may use or customize templates to suit their policy needs" lets programs adapt templates, P85.
units.anchor: Individual programs may use or customize templates to suit their policy needs

units.why: "Each instructor will have a statement in the syllabus about using AI" requires a graduate syllabus statement, P09.
units.anchor: Each instructor will have a statement in the syllabus about using AI

units.why: "Research supervisors and mentors will have a written statement about how AI may or may not be used in research" requires a written AI rule for supervised research, P62.
units.anchor: written statement about how AI may or may not be used in research

units.why: "discuss the policy and AI use with student and other research collaborators frequently" requires frequent discussion, P66.
units.anchor: discuss the policy and AI use with student and other research collaborators frequently

units.why: "receive acknowledgement from students/supervised researchers that they understand the supervisor’s expectations" has supervisors collect student acknowledgement, which no type covers.
units.anchor: receive acknowledgement from students/supervised researchers that they understand
units.uncovered_note: Supervisors must obtain students' acknowledgement that they understand the supervisor's AI expectations.

units.why: "Academic units will have a written statement about how AI may or may not be used in the process and products of qualifying and comprehensive exams" requires an exam AI statement, P09.
units.anchor: statement about how AI may or may not be used in the process and products
units.fit_note: Applies to qualifying and comprehensive exams, set by the unit.

units.why: "Appropriate uses, tools, and disclosures of AI may vary by discipline" lets rules differ across units, P85.
units.anchor: Appropriate uses, tools, and disclosures of AI may vary by discipline.

units.why: "Academic units will have a written statement about how AI may or may not be used in capstone experiences" requires a capstone AI statement, P62.
units.anchor: written statement about how AI may or may not be used in capstone experiences

units.why: "different capstone experiences ... will have unique goals; thus, different AI guidelines" ties guidelines to goals, P83.
units.anchor: will have unique goals; thus, different AI guidelines

notes: Coder B. Course layer deferred in collect; no school or computing documents found. Provost sample statements are coded as units because they are policy language offered for adoption.
